history.q: Which ruler declared himself the first emperor of a unified China in 221 BCE?
history.fact: Qin Shi Huang's tomb near Xi'an is guarded by the Terracotta Army, thousands of life-size clay soldiers found by farmers digging a well in 1974.

history.q: What was the last imperial dynasty to rule China?
history.fact: The Qing dynasty ended in 1912 when the six-year-old emperor Puyi abdicated, closing more than 2,000 years of imperial rule.

history.q: Kublai Khan founded which dynasty to rule China?
history.fact: Kublai Khan built his capital, Khanbaliq ('City of the Khan'), on the site of modern Beijing; Marco Polo described its splendour under the name Cambaluc.

history.q: In which year was the People's Republic of China founded?
history.fact: The People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 October 1949, a date celebrated every year as National Day with a week-long holiday known as Golden Week.

history.q: Which Ming dynasty admiral led seven great 'treasure fleet' voyages across the Indian Ocean?
history.fact: Between 1405 and 1433 Zheng He's fleets sailed as far as the Arabian Peninsula and East Africa, and brought back a giraffe as a gift for the emperor.

history.q: Which treaty, ending the First Opium War in 1842, ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain?
history.fact: The Treaty of Nanking also opened five ports, including Shanghai, to British trade, helping transform Shanghai into a global trading hub.

history.q: Which 1911 revolution overthrew the Qing dynasty?
history.fact: The Xinhai Revolution began with the Wuchang Uprising on 10 October 1911; 'Xinhai' is the name of that year in the traditional 60-year cycle.

history.q: Who is the only woman to have ruled China as emperor in her own name?
history.fact: Wu Zetian declared her own Zhou dynasty in 690, interrupting the Tang dynasty, and even invented new Chinese characters, including one for her own name.

history.q: Which Han dynasty envoy's missions to Central Asia in the 2nd century BCE helped open the Silk Road?
history.fact: Sent west by Emperor Wu around 138 BCE, Zhang Qian was captured by the Xiongnu and held for about ten years before completing his journey.

history.q: Under which short-lived dynasty were existing waterways linked to form the Grand Canal in the early 600s?
history.fact: The Grand Canal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2014, runs roughly 1,800 km between Beijing and Hangzhou and is among the world's longest artificial waterways.

history.q: Which philosopher, born in the state of Lu around 551 BCE, became China's most influential teacher of ethics?
history.fact: Confucius's sayings were compiled by his followers in the Analects; his hometown of Qufu still holds a vast temple and family cemetery in his honour.

history.q: What name is given to the Red Army's epic 1934-35 retreat that helped bring Mao Zedong to the leadership?
history.fact: The Long March took the Red Army about a year and thousands of kilometres across rivers and snowy mountain passes, ending in Shaanxi province in October 1935.

history.q: Most of the Great Wall that visitors walk on today was built during which dynasty?
history.fact: A 2012 Chinese government survey measured all historical sections of the Great Wall together at about 21,196 km, far longer than the Ming wall alone.

history.q: Which dynasty, ruling from 206 BCE to 220 CE, gave its name to China's majority ethnic group?
history.fact: Chinese characters are called hanzi, 'Han characters', after the same dynasty; in Japanese they became known as kanji.

history.q: What was the name of the political campaign launched by Mao Zedong in 1966 that lasted until 1976?
history.fact: During the Cultural Revolution, millions of urban 'educated youth' were sent to live and work in the countryside in the 'Up to the Mountains and Down to the Villages' movement.

history.q: Which 1958-1962 campaign aimed to rapidly industrialise China through communes and mass steel production?
history.fact: The campaign encouraged villages to make steel in backyard furnaces; it was followed by a severe famine in which tens of millions of people died.

history.q: Which 1919 student protest movement in Beijing was sparked by the Treaty of Versailles?
history.fact: The protests began on 4 May 1919, when some 3,000 students gathered at Tiananmen against the transfer of Germany's rights in Shandong to Japan.

history.q: Which 1850-1864 rebellion was led by Hong Xiuquan, who claimed to be the younger brother of Jesus?
history.fact: The Taiping set up their 'Heavenly Kingdom' with its capital at Nanjing; the war was one of the deadliest conflicts of the 19th century.

history.q: Which anti-foreign uprising of 1899-1901 ended when an eight-nation force relieved the besieged foreign legations in Beijing?
history.fact: The Boxers got their English name from their martial-arts practices; in Chinese they called themselves the Yihetuan, 'Militia United in Righteousness'.

history.q: Which empress dowager effectively controlled the Qing government for nearly half a century until her death in 1908?
history.fact: Cixi entered the palace as a low-ranking concubine of the Xianfeng Emperor; her son became the Tongzhi Emperor in 1861.

history.q: Which dynasty left the earliest known Chinese writing, carved on 'oracle bones'?
history.fact: Oracle bones were often ox shoulder blades or turtle shells; diviners heated them, read the cracks, then carved the questions and answers into them.

history.q: Which Han dynasty historian wrote the 'Records of the Grand Historian' (Shiji)?
history.fact: Sima Qian was castrated as punishment for defending a disgraced general; he accepted the sentence rather than suicide so he could finish his history.

history.q: The 1689 Treaty of Nerchinsk was the Qing dynasty's first treaty with which European power?
history.fact: The Treaty of Nerchinsk had an official Latin text, drafted with help from Jesuit interpreters serving at the Qing court.

history.q: What was the capital of the Tang dynasty, then one of the largest cities in the world?
history.fact: Chang'an sat at the eastern end of the Silk Road; the modern city on the site is Xi'an, home of the Tang-era Big Wild Goose Pagoda.

history.q: Which rebellion of 755-763 severely weakened the Tang dynasty?
history.fact: An Lushan, a frontier general of Sogdian-Turkic descent, declared himself emperor in 756 but was murdered by his own son the following year.

technology.q: Which explosive mixture was developed by Chinese alchemists, reportedly while seeking an elixir of immortality?
technology.fact: The earliest known written formula for gunpowder appears in the Wujing Zongyao, a Song dynasty military manual compiled in 1044.

technology.q: The Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest power station by installed capacity, spans which river?
technology.fact: The Three Gorges Dam has an installed capacity of about 22.5 gigawatts, and its ship lift can raise vessels over 100 metres in one go.

technology.q: Which luxurious fabric originated in ancient China, spun from the cocoons of a moth caterpillar?
technology.fact: Silk was so prized that the trade routes linking China to the Mediterranean were later named the 'Silk Road' by a 19th-century German geographer.

technology.q: Which ceramic, so closely tied to the country that English simply calls it 'china', was perfected by Chinese potters?
technology.fact: Jingdezhen, China's 'porcelain capital', takes its name from the Song emperor's Jingde era (1004-1007), when its kilns supplied the imperial court.

technology.q: Which Han dynasty court official is traditionally credited with improving papermaking around 105 CE?
technology.fact: Cai Lun's paper used tree bark, hemp, old rags and fishing nets, making a cheap writing surface far lighter than bamboo strips.

technology.q: Who invented movable type printing using fired clay characters in the 1040s?
technology.fact: We know of Bi Sheng's invention thanks to the scholar Shen Kuo, who described it in his 'Dream Pool Essays', around four centuries before Gutenberg.

technology.q: Who became the first Chinese astronaut in space, aboard Shenzhou 5 in 2003?
technology.fact: Yang Liwei's flight made China the third country to send a person into orbit on its own rocket, after the Soviet Union and the United States.

technology.q: Tu Youyou won the 2015 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering a treatment for which disease?
technology.fact: Tu Youyou found the key to extracting artemisinin from sweet wormwood in a 4th-century medical text by the alchemist Ge Hong.

technology.q: Which Han dynasty polymath built a seismoscope to detect distant earthquakes in 132 CE?
technology.fact: Zhang Heng's bronze vessel had eight dragons; a quake would make one drop a ball into a toad's mouth below, hinting at the tremor's direction.

technology.q: The 5th-century mathematician Zu Chongzhi calculated which constant to seven decimal places?
technology.fact: Zu Chongzhi also gave the fraction 355/113 for pi, an approximation so good it was not bettered anywhere for nearly a millennium.

technology.q: Which navigation instrument, using a magnetised needle, was first described in China?
technology.fact: Shen Kuo described a magnetised needle compass in 1088, and by the early 1100s Chinese sailors were recorded using compasses at sea.

technology.q: Which Chinese technology company was founded by Ren Zhengfei in Shenzhen in 1987?
technology.fact: Huawei began by reselling telephone switches and grew into one of the world's largest makers of telecoms equipment.

technology.q: Which e-commerce giant was founded by Jack Ma in Hangzhou in 1999?
technology.fact: Alibaba turned Singles' Day on 11 November, a date chosen because 11/11 looks like four 'bare sticks', into the world's biggest shopping festival.

technology.q: Which counting device, with beads sliding on rods, has been used in China for centuries?
technology.fact: The traditional Chinese abacus, or suanpan, has two beads above the bar and five below; abacus calculation joined UNESCO's heritage list in 2013.

technology.q: Which Chinese company owns the short-video app TikTok?
technology.fact: ByteDance launched Douyin, its Chinese short-video app, in 2016, a year before the international version that became TikTok.

technology.q: What is the name of China's satellite navigation system, an alternative to GPS?
technology.fact: BeiDou is named after the Big Dipper constellation, long used to find north; its global system was completed in 2020.

technology.q: Which sea crossing, opened in 2018, links Hong Kong, Macau and Zhuhai across the Pearl River estuary?
technology.fact: The 55-km crossing includes a 6.7-km undersea tunnel between two artificial islands, leaving the shipping lanes above it clear.

technology.q: What is the name of the 500-metre radio telescope completed in Guizhou province in 2016?
technology.fact: FAST, nicknamed Tianyan ('Eye of Heaven'), sits in a natural karst hollow; its dish is about the size of 30 football pitches.

technology.q: Which Chinese city's maglev, in service since the early 2000s, was the world's first commercial high-speed maglev line?
technology.fact: Built with German Transrapid technology, the Shanghai Maglev has carried passengers at up to 431 km/h on its 30-km route to Pudong Airport.

technology.q: Under which dynasty did the Chinese government first issue paper money, in the 11th century?
technology.fact: The first paper notes, called jiaozi, began among Sichuan merchants who found iron coins too heavy; the Song government took over issuing them in the 1020s.

technology.q: Which Qin-state official designed the Dujiangyan irrigation system, still in use after more than 2,000 years?
technology.fact: Built around 256 BCE, Dujiangyan divides the Min River without a dam and still waters the Chengdu Plain; it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

technology.q: Which Song dynasty polymath built a water-powered astronomical clock tower in Kaifeng around 1090?
technology.fact: Su Song's clock tower used an early escapement mechanism, and his illustrated manual was detailed enough for modern engineers to build working replicas.

technology.q: Which Chinese scientist is known as the 'father of hybrid rice'?
technology.fact: Yuan Longping developed the first high-yielding hybrid rice in the 1970s; varieties based on his work are now grown across Asia, Africa and the Americas.

technology.q: Which scientist, a co-founder of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California, returned to China in 1955 to lead its rocket programme?
technology.fact: Qian Xuesen spent about five years under house arrest in the US during the McCarthy era before he was allowed to leave for China in 1955.

technology.q: Which Chinese supercomputer topped the world's TOP500 ranking from 2016 to 2018?
technology.fact: Sunway TaihuLight, in Wuxi, was the first supercomputer to top the world rankings using only Chinese-designed processors.

art.q: Which classic Chinese novel follows the monk Xuanzang on a pilgrimage with Sun Wukong, the Monkey King?
art.fact: Journey to the West, usually attributed to Wu Cheng'en in the 16th century, is based on a real monk who walked to India in the 7th century.

art.q: Which traditional theatre form, famous for its painted faces and acrobatics, is named after China's capital?
art.fact: Peking opera blends singing, speech, mime and martial arts, and was inscribed on UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2010.

art.q: Which two-stringed bowed instrument is sometimes called the 'Chinese violin'?
art.fact: On an erhu the bow's hair passes between the two strings, so the bow and instrument are effectively inseparable while being played.

art.q: Beijing's Forbidden City served as the imperial palace for which two dynasties?
art.fact: Built between 1406 and 1420 under the Yongle Emperor, the Forbidden City has housed the Palace Museum since 1925.

art.q: Which Tang dynasty poet is celebrated as the 'Immortal Poet'?
art.fact: A popular legend claims Li Bai drowned after leaning out of a boat to embrace the moon's reflection in the river.

art.q: Which 4th-century master, author of the 'Orchid Pavilion Preface', is revered as the 'Sage of Calligraphy'?
art.fact: Tang Emperor Taizong adored Wang Xizhi's Orchid Pavilion Preface so much that the original is said to have been buried with him.

art.q: Which film director staged the opening ceremony of the 2008 Beijing Olympics?
art.fact: Zhang Yimou's first film as director, Red Sorghum, won the Golden Bear at the 1988 Berlin Film Festival.

art.q: Which Chinese author won the 2012 Nobel Prize in Literature?
art.fact: The pen name Mo Yan means 'don't speak', a reminder of warnings he received as a child to be careful what he said.

art.q: Which Song dynasty artist painted the famous scroll 'Along the River During the Qingming Festival'?
art.fact: The handscroll, over 5 metres long, captures bustling street life in Kaifeng, then the Northern Song capital, with hundreds of tiny figures.

art.q: Who is credited as the author of the 18th-century novel 'Dream of the Red Chamber'?
art.fact: Dream of the Red Chamber is so intensively studied that its scholarship has a name of its own: 'Redology' (hongxue).

art.q: Which martial-arts star led the 1973 film 'Enter the Dragon'?
art.fact: Bruce Lee was born in San Francisco in 1940 but grew up in Hong Kong, where he worked as a child film actor.

art.q: Which ancient military treatise is attributed to Sun Tzu?
art.fact: The Art of War has 13 chapters; its best-known line says that if you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear a hundred battles.

art.q: Which classic novel, set at the end of the Han dynasty, tells of heroes such as Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Cao Cao?
art.fact: Attributed to Luo Guanzhong, the novel opens: 'The empire, long divided, must unite; long united, must divide.'

art.q: Beijing's Temple of Heaven was where emperors prayed for what?
art.fact: The Temple of Heaven's grounds have a rounded northern wall and a square southern one, reflecting the old belief that heaven is round and earth is square.

art.q: Chinese calligraphers traditionally write with which tool?
art.fact: The brush is one of the 'Four Treasures of the Study', alongside ink, paper and the inkstone on which the ink is ground.

art.q: Which pianist, born in Shenyang in 1982, performed at the opening ceremony of the 2008 Beijing Olympics?
art.fact: At the 2008 opening ceremony Lang Lang shared the piano with Li Muzi, a five-year-old girl.

art.q: Which giant Buddha was carved into a cliff above three rivers in Sichuan during the Tang dynasty?
art.fact: The Leshan Giant Buddha is about 71 metres tall; carving began in 713 and took around 90 years to complete.

art.q: Which Tang dynasty poet, a friend of Li Bai, is revered as the 'Sage Poet'?
art.fact: Du Fu's thatched cottage in Chengdu, where he lived for several years and wrote hundreds of poems, is now a museum and park.

art.q: Which classic novel follows 108 outlaws who gather at Mount Liang?
art.fact: Water Margin is one of the Four Great Classical Novels of Chinese literature and has inspired countless films, comics and video games.

art.q: Which director's 'Farewell My Concubine' shared the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 1993?
art.fact: Farewell My Concubine follows two Peking opera performers across half a century; it shared the 1993 Palme d'Or with Jane Campion's 'The Piano'.

art.q: Which Yuan dynasty painter created the landscape scroll 'Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains'?
art.fact: The scroll was partly burned in 1650 and split in two; its halves, kept in Hangzhou and Taipei, were shown together in 2011.

art.q: Which Song dynasty poet and statesman wrote the 'Former Ode on the Red Cliff'?
art.fact: Su Shi's pen name was Dongpo, and Dongpo pork, a slow-braised pork belly dish, is named after him.

art.q: Which 20th-century painter was famed for lively ink paintings of shrimp?
art.fact: Qi Baishi trained as a carpenter before becoming a painter; in 2017 a set of his landscape screens sold at auction for about US$140 million.

art.q: Which Ming dynasty play by Tang Xianzu is the best-known work of Kunqu opera?
art.fact: Tang Xianzu completed The Peony Pavilion in 1598 and died in 1616, the same year as Shakespeare.

art.q: The Mogao Caves, famed for Buddhist murals, lie near which Silk Road oasis city?
art.fact: A sealed 'Library Cave' at Mogao held tens of thousands of manuscripts, including a Diamond Sutra of 868, the oldest dated printed book.

politics.q: Who proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China from Tiananmen in 1949?
politics.fact: Tiananmen means 'Gate of Heavenly Peace'; the gate was first built in the 15th century as the entrance to the imperial city.

politics.q: Which leader launched China's 'Reform and Opening Up' policy in 1978?
politics.fact: In 1980 the fishing town of Shenzhen became one of China's first Special Economic Zones; it is now a metropolis of over 17 million people.

politics.q: In which year was Hong Kong transferred from British to Chinese sovereignty?
politics.fact: The handover took place on 1 July 1997; two years later, in December 1999, Macau was returned to China by Portugal.

politics.q: What is the name of China's national legislature?
politics.fact: With nearly 3,000 deputies, the National People's Congress is the largest parliamentary body in the world.

politics.q: What is the name of China's cabinet, the chief administrative body headed by the Premier?
politics.fact: The State Council oversees China's ministries and commissions and meets in the Zhongnanhai compound, next to the Forbidden City.

politics.q: Who served as the first Premier of the People's Republic of China, from 1949 until 1976?
politics.fact: Zhou Enlai was also foreign minister from 1949 to 1958 and hosted US President Richard Nixon's landmark visit to China in 1972.

politics.q: What is the official status of Hong Kong and Macau within the People's Republic of China?
politics.fact: Both Special Administrative Regions issue their own currencies: the Hong Kong dollar and the Macanese pataca.

politics.q: In which year did Xi Jinping become General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party?
politics.fact: Xi Jinping became Party General Secretary in November 2012 and was elected the country's President by the National People's Congress in March 2013.

politics.q: In which year was the current Constitution of the People's Republic of China adopted?
politics.fact: China has had four constitutions (1954, 1975, 1978 and 1982); the 1982 version has been amended five times, most recently in 2018.

politics.q: How many members has the Communist Party's Politburo Standing Committee had since 2012?
politics.fact: From 2002 to 2012 the Politburo Standing Committee had nine members; the 18th Party Congress in 2012 reduced it to seven.

politics.q: Which revolutionary became the first provisional president of the Republic of China in 1912?
politics.fact: Sun Yat-sen is honoured in both mainland China and Taiwan; his mausoleum stands on Purple Mountain in Nanjing.

politics.q: How many yellow stars appear on the flag of the People's Republic of China?
politics.fact: The Five-star Red Flag was designed by Zeng Liansong, an ordinary citizen who entered a public design competition held in 1949.

politics.q: Which Nationalist leader moved his Republic of China government to Taiwan in 1949?
politics.fact: Chiang Kai-shek succeeded Sun Yat-sen as leader of the Kuomintang and led the Northern Expedition of 1926-28 to unify China under the Nationalists.

politics.q: Which large public square in central Beijing contains Mao Zedong's mausoleum?
politics.fact: The Great Hall of the People, where the National People's Congress meets, lines the western side of Tiananmen Square.

politics.q: Which principle, proposed by Deng Xiaoping, governs Hong Kong's relationship with mainland China?
politics.fact: The principle allowed Hong Kong to keep its own legal system, currency and capitalist economy after the 1997 handover.

politics.q: In which city was the Chinese Communist Party founded in 1921?
politics.fact: The first Party congress met in Shanghai's French Concession in July 1921 but moved to a boat on South Lake in Jiaxing to finish.

politics.q: Who served as General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party from 1989 to 2002?
politics.fact: Jiang Zemin had previously been mayor and Party Secretary of Shanghai; his signature theory was the 'Three Represents'.

politics.q: Who was President of the People's Republic of China from 2003 to 2013?
politics.fact: Hu Jintao's guiding idea was the 'Scientific Outlook on Development'; his Premier for both terms was Wen Jiabao.

politics.q: What is the popular name for the annual March meetings of the National People's Congress and the CPPCC?
politics.fact: The CPPCC is a political advisory body whose members include the eight minor parties legally recognised in China.

politics.q: Which body commands China's armed forces, including the People's Liberation Army?
politics.fact: Technically there are two Central Military Commissions, one of the Party and one of the state, but their membership is identical.

politics.q: Who succeeded Mao Zedong as Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party in 1976?
politics.fact: Hua Guofeng had been chosen by Mao; within weeks of Mao's death he oversaw the arrest of the 'Gang of Four'.

politics.q: Which 1898 reform programme, backed by the Guangxu Emperor, was ended by a conservative coup after about three months?
politics.fact: After the reform failed, the Guangxu Emperor spent the rest of his life under palace confinement, while reformer Kang Youwei fled abroad.

politics.q: In which year did the People's Republic of China take China's seat at the United Nations?
politics.fact: UN General Assembly Resolution 2758 of October 1971 gave the China seat, including its permanent place on the Security Council, to the People's Republic.

politics.q: Which city was the capital of the Republic of China for most of the period from 1927 to 1949?
politics.fact: During the war with Japan, the Nationalist government moved to Chongqing, which served as its wartime capital until 1946.

politics.q: What is the name of Hong Kong's constitutional document, in force since 1997?
politics.fact: The Basic Law was adopted by the National People's Congress in 1990; the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration had set out the handover terms.

current-affairs.q: Which city hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics, becoming the first to host both Summer and Winter Games?
current-affairs.fact: Beijing's 2022 Games reused 2008 venues: the 'Water Cube' swimming centre was converted into the 'Ice Cube' for curling.

current-affairs.q: According to UN estimates, which country overtook China in 2023 as the world's most populous?
current-affairs.fact: China's National Bureau of Statistics reported that the population fell in 2022, the first decline since 1961.

current-affairs.q: In 2024, China's Chang'e 6 mission became the first to return samples from where?
choices: The far side of the Moon
current-affairs.fact: Chang'e 6 collected its samples in the South Pole-Aitken basin, one of the largest known impact craters in the Solar System.

current-affairs.q: Which Hangzhou-based artificial intelligence company released its R1 reasoning model in January 2025?
current-affairs.fact: DeepSeek's release briefly made its app the top free download on Apple's US App Store and sent shockwaves through global tech stocks.

current-affairs.q: What was the name of the rover China landed on Mars in May 2021?
current-affairs.fact: Zhurong, named after a fire god in Chinese mythology, touched down on the plain of Utopia Planitia as part of the Tianwen-1 mission.

current-affairs.q: Who became Premier of China in March 2023, succeeding Li Keqiang?
current-affairs.fact: Before becoming Premier, Li Qiang served as the Communist Party Secretary of Shanghai, China's largest city.

current-affairs.q: Which city hosted the Asian Games held in 2023, postponed from 2022?
current-affairs.fact: Hangzhou is famed for West Lake, a UNESCO World Heritage Site whose misty scenery has inspired Chinese poets and painters for centuries.

current-affairs.q: Which Chinese-built narrow-body airliner made its first commercial passenger flight in May 2023?
current-affairs.fact: The C919's first commercial flight was operated by China Eastern Airlines, carrying passengers from Shanghai to Beijing.

current-affairs.q: What is the name of the core module of China's Tiangong space station, launched in 2021?
current-affairs.fact: Tiangong means 'Heavenly Palace'; the station was completed in 2022 when the Wentian and Mengtian laboratory modules joined Tianhe.

current-affairs.q: How many gold medals did China win at the 2024 Paris Olympics, level with the United States for the most?
current-affairs.fact: At Paris 2024 China's divers won all eight Olympic diving events, the first clean sweep of the sport at a single Games.

current-affairs.q: In which Chinese city were the first cases of COVID-19 reported in December 2019?
current-affairs.fact: Wuhan straddles the Yangtze and Han rivers and is known for re gan mian, 'hot dry noodles', a popular breakfast dish.

current-affairs.q: Which Chinese animated film became the highest-grossing animated film of all time in 2025?
current-affairs.fact: Ne Zha 2 overtook Disney's Inside Out 2 to become the top-grossing animated film ever, earning over US$2 billion, mostly in China.

current-affairs.q: Which Shenzhen-based carmaker overtook Tesla in the last quarter of 2023 as the world's top seller of fully electric cars?
current-affairs.fact: BYD began in 1995 as a maker of rechargeable batteries; its initials were later given the slogan 'Build Your Dreams'.

current-affairs.q: China's seventh national census, carried out in 2020, recorded a mainland population of roughly how many people?
current-affairs.fact: The 2020 census found Guangdong to be China's most populous province, with more than 126 million residents.

current-affairs.q: In 2024, which animals did China send to San Diego Zoo and Washington's National Zoo under new conservation agreements?
current-affairs.fact: Washington's National Zoo welcomed pandas Bao Li and Qing Bao in October 2024, less than a year after its previous pandas returned to China.

current-affairs.q: Which Chinese player won the women's singles tennis gold medal at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
current-affairs.fact: Zheng Qinwen's victory made her the first Asian player, man or woman, to win an Olympic singles tennis title.

current-affairs.q: Which Chinese city hosted the Asian Winter Games held in February 2025?
current-affairs.fact: Harbin is famed for its Ice and Snow Festival, where huge sculptures and buildings are carved from blocks of ice cut from the Songhua River.

current-affairs.q: Which Chinese mission brought lunar samples back to Earth in December 2020?
current-affairs.fact: Chang'e 5 returned about 1.7 kg of lunar rock and soil, the first Moon samples brought to Earth since the Soviet Luna 24 in 1976.

current-affairs.q: Which Chinese swimmer set a world record while winning the men's 100 m freestyle at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
current-affairs.fact: Pan Zhanle won in 46.40 seconds, becoming the first Chinese man to win Olympic gold in the 100 m freestyle.

current-affairs.q: Which video game from Chinese studio Game Science, starring the Monkey King, sold over 10 million copies within days of its August 2024 release?
current-affairs.fact: Many of Black Myth: Wukong's settings were modelled on real Chinese temples and pagodas, which saw a surge of visitors after the game's release.

current-affairs.q: Which Sichuan city hosted the Summer World University Games held in 2023?
current-affairs.fact: Chengdu is home to the Giant Panda Breeding Research Base, which opened in 1987 with six pandas rescued from the wild.

current-affairs.q: What name was given to China's third aircraft carrier, launched in Shanghai in June 2022?
current-affairs.fact: Fujian was China's first carrier designed with electromagnetic catapults, a launch system previously used only on the US Navy's Gerald R. Ford class.

current-affairs.q: Which Chinese diver won the Olympic women's 10 m platform gold in 2021 and again in 2024?
current-affairs.fact: Quan Hongchan was just 14 in Tokyo, where three of her five dives drew perfect 10s from every judge; Chen Yuxi took silver both times.

current-affairs.q: On which mission did Wang Yaping become the first Chinese woman to walk in space, in November 2021?
current-affairs.fact: The Shenzhou 13 crew spent about six months aboard the Tiangong station, China's longest crewed mission at the time.

current-affairs.q: In which capital city did Saudi Arabia and Iran sign their March 2023 agreement to restore diplomatic relations?
current-affairs.fact: The agreement ended a seven-year rift: Saudi Arabia and Iran had cut diplomatic ties in 2016.

general.q: Which river is often called the 'cradle of Chinese civilisation' and the 'Mother River'?
general.fact: The Yellow River gets its colour and name from the vast amounts of fine loess silt it carries from China's Loess Plateau.

general.q: What is the main unit of China's currency, the renminbi?
general.fact: Renminbi literally means 'the people's currency'; the yuan is its basic unit, just as the pound is the unit of sterling.

general.q: In China, Chinese New Year is also known as what?
general.fact: Spring Festival celebrations traditionally end on the 15th day of the new year with the Lantern Festival, when people solve riddles written on lanterns.

general.q: Mount Everest sits on the border between China and which country?
general.fact: In 2020 China and Nepal jointly announced a new official height for Everest: 8,848.86 metres.

general.q: Which province is home to most of the world's wild giant pandas?
general.fact: Sichuan's Giant Panda Sanctuaries, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2006, protect more than 30% of the world's pandas.

general.q: How many official time zones does China use?
general.fact: Although China spans about five geographical time zones, the whole country runs on Beijing Time (UTC+8), so dawn in far-western Xinjiang can come after 9 a.m.

general.q: Which city is famous for roast duck served with thin pancakes, spring onion and sweet bean sauce?
general.fact: Quanjude, one of Beijing's best-known roast duck restaurants, was founded in 1864 during the Qing dynasty.

general.q: What is the standard spoken Chinese promoted nationwide called in mainland China?
general.fact: Putonghua means 'common speech'. Its Latin-alphabet spelling system, Pinyin, was officially adopted in 1958.

general.q: What is the largest desert lying entirely within China?
general.fact: The Taklamakan fills the Tarim Basin in Xinjiang; Silk Road caravans skirted its northern and southern edges rather than cross its shifting dunes.

general.q: Which Chinese city is nicknamed the 'Spring City' for its mild climate all year round?
general.fact: Kunming, capital of Yunnan, sits about 1,900 metres above sea level, which keeps it from getting very hot in summer or very cold in winter.

general.q: Which animal comes first in the 12-year cycle of the Chinese zodiac?
general.fact: Legend says the zodiac order was set by a great race; the clever Rat rode on the Ox's back and leapt ahead at the finish line.

general.q: Which slow, flowing martial art, practised by millions in parks for exercise, joined UNESCO's heritage list in 2020?
general.fact: Tai chi is traditionally traced to Chenjiagou, the Chen family village in Henan province, where the Chen style developed in the 17th century.

general.q: Which Chinese city is famous for the Bund waterfront and the Oriental Pearl Tower?
general.fact: Across the river from the Bund, Pudong was largely farmland before the 1990s; it is now home to Shanghai Tower, China's tallest building at 632 m.

general.q: Which river is the longest in Asia?
general.fact: The Yangtze runs about 6,300 km from the Tibetan Plateau to the East China Sea at Shanghai, making it the third-longest river in the world.

general.q: Which crescent-shaped dumplings are traditionally eaten on Chinese New Year's Eve in northern China?
general.fact: Jiaozi are said to resemble ancient silver ingots, so eating them at New Year is a wish for wealth in the year ahead.

general.q: Which region is the largest province-level division of China by area?
general.fact: Xinjiang covers about one-sixth of China's territory and borders eight countries, more than any other province-level region.

general.q: Which mountain range in Anhui, famed for granite peaks, twisted pines and seas of cloud, inspired generations of landscape painters?
general.fact: Huangshan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1990, has 72 named peaks; the tallest, Lotus Peak, rises 1,864 metres.

general.q: Weiqi, the ancient Chinese board game of surrounding territory, is better known in the West by which Japanese-derived name?
general.fact: In 2016 Google DeepMind's AlphaGo beat champion Lee Sedol 4-1, a landmark for AI in a game long thought too complex for computers.

general.q: What is China's best-known clear spirit, usually distilled from sorghum?
general.fact: Moutai, a sorghum baijiu from Guizhou province, is served at Chinese state banquets and its maker is among the world's most valuable drinks companies.

general.q: Which Chinese player became the first from an Asian country to win a Grand Slam singles title, at the 2011 French Open?
general.fact: Li Na added the 2014 Australian Open title and in 2019 became the first Asian-born player inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

general.q: What is China's largest freshwater lake?
general.fact: Poyang Lake in Jiangxi swells in the summer rainy season and shrinks in winter, when it becomes a key wintering ground for Siberian cranes.

general.q: Which mountain in Shandong was the most revered of China's Five Great Mountains, where emperors performed sacrifices to heaven?
general.fact: Climbing Mount Tai's more than 6,000 stone steps to the summit has been a pilgrimage for centuries; it was listed by UNESCO in 1987.

general.q: The karst scenery on the back of China's 20-yuan banknote shows the Li River near which city?
general.fact: The Li River's limestone peaks between Guilin and Yangshuo are among China's most painted and photographed landscapes.

general.q: Which famous pan-fired green tea comes from the hills around Hangzhou?
general.fact: Longjing, or 'Dragon Well', tea is pressed by hand in hot woks, which gives its leaves their distinctive flat, smooth shape.

general.q: Which gorge, among the deepest in the world, is cut by the Jinsha River in Yunnan?
general.fact: Legend says a tiger escaping a hunter leapt across the river at the gorge's narrowest point, using a large rock in mid-stream.
